A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VISCOP study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and matchable despite reformatting, renumbering, and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-domain adaptation experiments, simulated and real-world robotics results, ablations, and representation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds audio adaptation, additional baselines, interaction-scope ablations, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The core layerwise probing, connectors, and autoregressive objective remain unchanged. v2 additionally describes a spectrogram-input instantiation that repurposes the vision encoder into a universal audio/video encoder (Table 8 discussion), constituting a limited modality-specific adaptation.

E1.justification: v2 adds MusicAVQA, using audio-centric questions as the target and video-centric questions as the source. This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained egocentric, depth, and robotic-control settings. Ego-in-Exo PerceptionMCQ's shortened name does not establish another dataset addition.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds evaluated VPT and Model Tailor comparisons alongside the retained VP, LoRA, Last-4, and QFormer-style alternatives. Appendix A.4 additionally compares against source-data replay and KL regularization, substantially broadening the comparison methods.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce audio-target/video-source evaluation, replay with 5%, 10%, and 25% source samples, KL-regularized training, and inference-cost measurements. The stated Ego-in-Exo evaluation count changes from 3,991 to 3,881 without establishing a rerun. Table 3 also reverses one robotics baseline's VE/LLM trainability labels, conflicting with the retained configuration in Appendix Table 12.

E4.justification: v2 adds spatial-only versus temporal-only versus joint probing ablations (Table 6), computational-overhead analysis (Table 7), and retention controls testing whether regularization explains the gains (Appendix A.4). Figure 8 extends probe-count sensitivity analysis from egocentric adaptation to depth and robotics; its egocentric panel repeats existing evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 real-robot trials per task and 95% fitted-Gaussian regions in the embedding visualization. v2 adds no training-seed counts, repeated-training-run reporting, performance confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for new comparators, interaction scopes, computational costs, audio adaptation, and cross-domain probe sensitivity. For example, Table 8 reports audio/source averages of 40.2/56.8 for VISCOP versus 39.8/52.2 for UE + LLM (LoRA). Original Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results. Table 5 changes VISCOP's source average/delta from 75.74/+2.12 to 76.19/+1.77, matching the retained detailed results.

T1.justification: The domain-risk formulation, cross-attention and projection equations, and autoregressive objective are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims: frozen-encoder visual probing improves target adaptation while preserving source capabilities across viewpoint, modality, and robotics shifts. The introduction's two-way-probing terminology reframes the existing visual-to-language pathway.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations concerning joint spatiotemporal information, retention regularization, shorter decoding, and excessive probes producing inappropriate robotic outputs. It also discusses applicability to audio. Its new claim of the smallest Bhattacharyya distance across all three domains overstates unchanged Figure 4c: egocentric VISCOP is 0.08 versus the base model's 0.07.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents base/VISCOP parameter counts, VRAM usage, and separate visual-extraction and full-model inference timings (Table 7), plus the spectrogram/universal-encoder setup. Existing learning rates, epochs, GPUs, LoRA rank, robotics collection details, and release promise remain. Detailed configurations for several new comparisons are still unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning against Head2Toe, visual and prefix prompt tuning, and Model Tailor, plus OneLLM and MusicAVQA references supporting the audio experiment. The ViViT citation is removed. These extend the existing positioning without replacing its central distinction between intermediate-feature probing and compression of frozen representations.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten around intermediate representations and two-way probing. The appendix reorganizes quantitative and qualitative material into a different subsection hierarchy, and explanatory passages are expanded throughout the diagnostics. The formal method and conclusion remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The document switches to a two-column layout and extensively redesigns table headers, component legends, and highlighting. The original Figures 3 and 4 become Figure 3(a,b); appendix tables are regrouped, and new analysis tables and probe-count panels are added. Existing architecture and qualitative figures are retained and repositioned.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the retention controls and interaction-scope ablations test important alternative explanations, while added baselines and computational measurements make the evidence more informative. These benefits support a net improvement, but sparse implementation details for new experiments and reporting errors limit it, particularly the contradictory robotics baseline labels and the overstated alignment interpretation.
